elaine (sec-eng): Heads up — discovered lifecycle transition on a few GCS backup buckets stripped our CMEK metadata. Re-encrypt job skipped them because it trusts the x-goog-meta-encryption flag. Logs and repro below.

mike (infra): timeline + scope?

elaine (sec-eng): Found at 02:45 UTC during routine spot-check. Affected: 2 prod tenant prefixes, 4 staging. Lifecycle rule changed storage class to NEARLINE and in at least one case a compose happened which dropped user metadata.

rachel (encops): compose/drop metadata is a known GCS quirk. Did the objects go through a compose/object-rewrite? Composed objects often lose custom headers unless explicitly preserved.

elaine (sec-eng): Repro (staging):
```
# upload multi-part snapshot
gsutil -m cp -r ./snapshots/2026-03-20 gs://redwood-backups/tenant-99/snapshots/
# lifecycle ran and composed parts into a single object
gsutil stat gs://redwood-backups/tenant-99/snapshots/2026-03-20/part-0001
```
Before lifecycle metadata:
```
x-goog-meta-encryption: CMEK
x-goog-meta-kms-key: projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/backup/cryptoKeys/tenant-99
```
After compose/transition:
```
x-goog-meta-encryption: sse
# x-goog-meta-kms-key missing
storage-class: NEARLINE
```

sam (sre): devops-bot: show re-encrypt job log around 03:00

devops-bot: re-encrypt-backups-03:00
```
INFO scanning bucket redwood-backups/tenant-99
INFO found object part-0001 storageClass=NEARLINE metadata.x-goog-meta-encryption=sse
INFO skip object part-0001 reason=metadata.indicates_encrypted
WARNING attempted_kms_wrap=false
```

rachel (encops): The skip heuristic is brittle. We should never rely solely on uploader-set metadata. Proposed immediate fixes:
- pause lifecycle transitions for affected buckets
- change re-encrypt job to validate by attempting a lightweight KMS envelope-check (HEAD/decrypt-check) when metadata says "encrypted"
- scan recent composed/rewritten objects

mike (infra): I'll disable the lifecycle rule on the two prod buckets now. Also we need to coordinate with storage team; a manual corrective rewrap is required for objects where the KMS key header was lost.

lucas (platform): Proposed re-encrypt job changes (PR in flight):
- detection: if x-goog-meta-encryption present, attempt KMS decrypt-check; if header missing but storageClass=NEARLINE and object age <48h, treat as potential candidate
- repair: use server-side object rewrite with kmsKeyName set (no plaintext egress)
- observability: emit audit log event `backup.rewrap.attempt` with object path and old/new metadata
PR: https://git.internal.redwood/repo/platform/pulls/542

elaine (sec-eng): Preventing customer-facing risk: add gating on restore flow that fails closed if object lacks CMEK envelope. Return error code ERR_RESTORED_OBJ_UNWRAPPED and queue rewrap action.

sam (sre): I'll run a scanner and generate a list. Runbook snippet I used:
```
# list candidate objects
gsutil ls -r gs://redwood-backups/tenant-*/snapshots/** | while read o; do
  meta=$(gsutil stat "$o" | grep x-goog-meta-encryption || true)
  sc=$(gsutil stat "$o" | grep "Storage Class" || true)
  if echo "$meta" | grep -q "CMEK" || (echo "$sc" | grep -q NEARLINE); then
    # attempt lightweight KMS envelope check via metadata/KMS API
    if ! curl -s -X POST "$KMS_API/wrapCheck" -d "{object:$o}" ; then
      echo "$o" >> /tmp/needs-rewrap
    fi
  fi
done
```

rachel (encops): Repair plan (safe, server-side):
1) Object-rewrite specifying kmsKeyName (GCS rewrite with kmsKeyName). This performs server-side re-encrypt without exposing plaintext.
2) Verify crc32c/md5 checksum post-rewrite matches (or validate via storage provider checksums).
3) Promote rewritten version atomically or update index to point to new generation.
We must NOT download plaintext to re-encrypt locally.

mike (infra): KMS QPS and billing concern: object-rewrite + KMS wrap calls will hit KMS. Throttle to 50 QPS per region and run per-tenant batches. Also alert customers if restore windows shift.

elaine (sec-eng): Compliance: notify auditors — small subset of backed-up objects temporarily lost CMEK envelope due to lifecycle composition. Rachel, can you draft an incident notification and include mitigation steps? We should include the scope, remediation timeline, and assurance that no plaintext was exposed.

rachel (encops): Draft ready. Will include:
- affected tenants and object counts
- immediate mitigations (lifecycle paused, rewrap in progress)
- audit log evidence of the transitions and rewrap attempts
- timeline for rewrap completion

oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-93 created (P2) 

sam (sre): Temporary alert rule: if lifecycle transition events + metadata-change > 5 objects in 1h for same bucket -> page SRE. I'll add rule and a 24h suppression window for known maintenance.

lucas (platform): Deployed a canary of re-encrypt job with new detection logic to staging. Will promote after 2h of stable runs.

mike (infra): Need a service account KMS grant for the rewrite worker for the affected key rings. Ping me with the SA names and I'll grant limited Encrypt/Decrypt for rewrap operations.

elaine (sec-eng): Action items summary:
- lucas: disable lifecycle on affected prod buckets (in progress)
- sam: run scanner, produce /tmp/needs-rewrap and start tenant-by-tenant rewrite
- lucas: deploy re-encrypt job patch to canary then prod
- mike: apply KMS grants and enforce QPS throttles
- rachel: incident notification for compliance
- all: update backup lifecycle docs to note metadata preservation caveats

elaine (sec-eng): tagging @oncall-bot for follow-ups :eyes:

oncall-bot: noted. Will post follow-up when rewrap complete or if escalation needed.

sam (sre): scanner running. Prioritizing NEARLINE objects with missing x-goog-meta-kms-key. Will update when /tmp/needs-rewrap populated.

lucas (platform): monitoring canary metrics and logs. :thumbsup:

mike (infra): if we hit any permission errors during rewrite, I'll rotate grants quickly. Ping me.

elaine (sec-eng): Thanks team. We'll hold a short postmortem once remediation done to update the runbook and lifecycle config guidance."
